top_stories.title: India eyes major bond index entry as tax exemptions sweeten appeal - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **finance ministry** are seeking to engage with the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)** as part of efforts to attract foreign investment in Indian government bonds.  The country is reapplying for inclusion in major global bond indices, aiming to bring $7-11 billion into India. These moves follow significant tax exemptions for foreign investors and expanded long-dated securities pools. Officials are also engaging with global index operators to address concerns about market access, settlement, and trade oversight.

top_stories.title: What the Pope talks about when he talks about human dignity | The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Pope Leo XIV** issued an encyclical titled "Magnifica Humanitas" that calls for governments to regulate AI companies, protect workers displaced by AI, and ensure human oversight of autonomous weapons. The encyclical also emphasizes the importance of a shared moral imagination and recognizing the inherent value of the human person. **Leo XIV**'s stance on technology challenges society to reflect on questions about human life and envision a civilization built on love.  The encyclical argues that democracy should go beyond being a political system and become an effort to create new humanizing values for peace and non-violence, acknowledging the dangers of uncontrolled AI manipulation and the need for apology and pacifism in order to achieve a just coexistence.

top_stories.title: In cotton fields, policy is undoing what science built. That’s the challenge for the Cotton Productivity Mission | The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Indian government** launched the Cotton Productivity Mission with an aim to increase lint productivity from 441 kg/ha to 755 kg/ha by 2031. However, this mission faces challenges as previous policies aimed at price control have stifled innovation in seed technology.  This has led to a decline in cotton production and India's inability to compete with other countries like Brazil, China, and Australia. The success of the Cotton Productivity Mission hinges on whether it can address these policy issues and foster private sector investment in new seed varieties.

top_stories.title: Why Iran has linked US peace deal more to Lebanon than to Gaza | Explained News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Iran** and **the US** have entered a stalemate in their 100-day conflict, with limited strikes at strategic targets and the Strait of Hormuz blocked.  **Iran** faces an urgent need to secure tangible gains from its leverage over the blockade, while **Washington** prefers to maintain its own blockade without escalating to a full-scale war. **Mohsen Rezaee**, advisor to the Supreme Leader, has warned that if **US** fails to unfreeze $24 billion in blocked Iranian assets and lift the blockade, Iran will expand its punitive actions to other regions.  Despite a ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon brokered by **the US**, **Iran** sees this as an opportunity to pressure **Washington** towards concessions.

top_stories.title: 40 years ago June 8, 1986: Ten shot dead in Punjab | The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ten** people were killed by suspected terrorists in Punjab over the past 24 hours, including **Rahim**, an Iranian student who was shot while seeking admission at **Punjabi University**.  The **Aid India** consortium will meet in Paris to discuss a new aid package for India, which is expected to be close to $3.9 billion. Queen Elizabeth II urged **Margaret Thatcher**, the British Prime Minister, to impose economic sanctions against South Africa.

top_stories.title: As Opposition attacks farm loan waiver conditions, Maharashtra govt’s own cabinet note says eligibility restrictions will reduce payout | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: Despite criticism from opposition parties, the **Maharashtra** government's new farm loan waiver scheme is projected to have a lower final expenditure than its initial outlay of Rs 36,585 crore. The scheme, which aims to provide debt relief to small and marginal farmers with crop loans, will be implemented in phases, with eligibility conditions including repayment of overdue amounts exceeding Rs 2 lakh or repaying dues above Rs 50,000 for previous loan waiver beneficiaries.  The government estimates that around 16.48 lakh farmers will benefit from the debt waiver component, while another 12.71 lakh farmers will receive an incentive of up to Rs 50,000 for regular loan repayment. The scheme excludes salaried individuals earning more than Rs 25,000 a month, income taxpayers, government employees, current and former elected representatives, and pensioners drawing more than Rs 25,000 a month.

top_stories.title: Iran war live: Israel bombs western, central Iran despite Trump appeal | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Israel** launched attacks on western and central **Iran**, following **Iran’s** missile strikes on Israel in response to Israeli attacks on Beirut. The US State Department issued a security alert for citizens in Jordan over reports of projectiles in the country's airspace.  **Iran** has called for diplomacy, while **Israel** faces pressure from the US not to retaliate against **Iran**.

top_stories.title: 33 years later, a conviction in Bihar’s Vaishali district - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Deep Rai**, an 85-year-old man, is serving a three-year prison sentence for attempted murder and violations of the Arms Act in Bihar's Vaishali district. He was convicted by the **Vaishali Court** on June 2, 2026, along with four other individuals. Rai's daughter, **Uma Devi**, attempts to provide comfort to her father amidst the sweltering heat and the lack of relief from the oppressive conditions.

top_stories.title: India eyes major bond index entry as tax exemptions sweeten appeal - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the finance ministry are seeking to attract foreign investment into Indian government bonds by engaging with the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)**.  The country is reapplying for inclusion in major global bond indices, aiming to bring in $7-11 billion. The move follows tax exemptions for foreign investors on capital gains and withholding taxes, as well as expanded long-dated securities pools. These efforts are expected to address concerns raised by global index operators regarding market access, settlement, and trade oversight, potentially leading to India's inclusion in the Bloomberg Global gauge.

top_stories.title: What the Dutch can teach the UK about tackling youth unemployment
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Alan Milburn**, former health secretary, warns that one in six young people could become Neet within five years unless urgent action is taken. The **Netherlands** has one of the lowest youth unemployment rates in the world, at 4.9% among 18 to 24-year-olds, and its approach to tackling youth engagement could be a model for the UK.  The Dutch system emphasizes a "no dead ends" philosophy, requiring children to stay in education or training until they either secure a qualification or turn 18. The Netherlands uses a combination of compulsory schooling, streaming into secondary tracks based on academic aptitude and vocational skills, and work-study pathways to connect young people with employment opportunities.  The Dutch system also provides support mechanisms for at-risk youth, including funding for specialized organizations and mental health services. Despite the success of this approach, youth unemployment is rising in the Netherlands, prompting the government to expand benefits and job search assistance programs.
